This is a classic, simple setup that works really well. Note that there isn't a lot of tonal differentiation between Heritage and the cognac mat, but you do get a play on the textures of the burl wood against the texture of the vegan leather. Breaking this up with wood racks introduces yet another natural texture and is beautiful.With wood racks, you can generally pick any tone/stain but here I would go for something in the oak family to get some contrast since the tiles and mat are close in color. Earthy, beautiful & simple. Works great if you want to keep a set out in a home decorated with a muted earthy palette or a speakeasy basement vibe - and men tend to really like this setup too!

The other version of Dapper is the current version, and as you can see the chocolate brown has printed to more of a deep merlot. The green is a bit more sage than hunter as well. This is the CURRENT dapper mat sold on OMM website.And YES it still works because it's all still muted and masculine but MAN I wish they would bring back Dapper 1 because I think it was a much better match. You can score Dapper 1 by asking around if anyone is selling their "original Dapper" mat on FB, that's how I scored mine. But if you can't find it I still think Dapper 2 is a great mat and works well with Heritage.

This mat doesn't get a lot of love because it has a very primary color red and not much pink to blend it to many OMM tiles aside from Nantucket. But Heritage works beautifully here with lots of blues and orangey-reds in its faces. The green layers pull in the leaves and the burl wood back pulls the honey tone of the bamboo border. Overall the Liberty mat feels classic and Americana and Heritage is a very sophisticated and classic tile so the vibes work well together.

The deep blues of Astor provide a beautiful backdrop for Heritage's orange/honey tones to really pop. And there are plenty of tonal oranges in the mat (peaches and creams with orange undertones) that blend it's colors into the mat. There are no greens in Astor but there are rust tones that find coordination in the faces.I love this mat because of the way it's patterns blend the masculine (plaid border) and feminine (floral and botanical center) in a deep moody, jewel tone colorway. It's not hard to see why Heritage works here then with a masculine tie to the plaid and juxtaposition against the floral center.Oak racks pick up on the butterscotch border and add another natural element to the Heritage burl or add tortoise for another beautiful layer of pattern.

Vanderbilt has a great earthy/muted color palette that works great with Heritage and just feels fall/winter to me. The buffalo check/plaid feels masculine and moody and works great with the vibe of Heritage. The honey orange tones of Heritage's burl wood against the deep navy and slate blues of Vanderbilt is a great complimentary pop. Love it with more pattern by layering tortoise or pulling in the butterscotch border with oak racks.

Love this combo, my favorite is with wood racks (of any tone really.) It's such a sophisticated and elegant setup that is neutral while still having some color with blue and green earth tones. And here Heritage again gives blue a complimentary pop of contrast with its honey/orange toned backs.

The bottom layer of Heritage is a sage green that is almost a dead ringer for the dominant sage green in this mat's perimeter. This mat is more muted than people realize when you really look at the tones of it but still has some brighter elements and a pastel pink center so Heritage and it's masculinity/earthy texture both blends and gives a great juxtaposition on this mat. People really respond to the complexity of this combo, especially with tortoise racks.

I feel like people either love or hate this mat. It has a bold art deco vibe that I personally love and think it couldn't be any more perfect than with Heritage. The true tone of Heritage is muted orange/brown so (just like Sierra,) you'll get maximum pop when you put orange on blue (it's complement, directly across on the color wheel) and I LOVE how simple the middle of the Soho mat is. But it's the layers and faces of Heritage that make it truly look made for this mat - pulling in Soho's greens, blues and rust orange accents PERFECTLY. I'm sad OMM is discontinuing this mat!

I think this is my favorite tile on Camellia. Kind of similar to what Heritage does on Citrus Songbird, it offers a great juxtaposition against Camellia's dainty, pretty, tea party vibe. Tortoise racks for the win to add complexity with layered patterns.

Orange is the complement of blue (opposite on the color wheel) and is therefore the color that will give the most pop. Sierra's orange is a burnt orange which makes it work with other muted and earthy colors like the butterscotch tone and deep plums and navy blues of Vanderbilt.

Luna also has a muted pallet primarily of blues with accents of a blue-green juniper. As a more muted earthy tile Sierra fits right in here, tortoise racks for the win to help balance the orange tones and again, a complimentary color pop of orange on blue.

If you learn the basics of the color wheel you'll know some combos will always work and more easily be able to understand why certain combos work. A good tip is to really pay attention to the dominant color of the center of the mat - where your tiles will be as you play - in this case navy blue. If you want to maximize your "pop" on the mat, pick the dominant color's complement on the color wheel, the color that sits opposite of it. For blue, it's orange.The next step is to match up what I call the clean/dirty factor. Some colors are fresh & clean, bright & airy - think pastels, brights, etc.... And other colors are dirtier, muddier, moodier and more muted. While it's not a hard and fast "rule", generally speaking matching up the same general tones of clean with clean and dirty with dirty will often work better. If you try to put OMM Sunset on this mat, you will quickly see the difference of a clean/bright orange and see that it makes Soho look dirty or Sunset look neon. Same for if you try to put Sierra onto the OMM Goldie mat - Sierra just looks dingy and off.This combo of Soho & Sierra is a great match for a pop of color in a colorful yet muted palette that's great for an Art Deco/Speakeasy vibe if that's your thing!

Britt Mills' new Haven mat is gorgeous and her watercolor always has a nice tonal range that make her mats pretty easy to match to.

I'm adding Oh My Mahjong's Heron mat to this album but am reserving judgement for an in person viewing. Heron is decidedly more of a mint green and not a lot of green tonal range here so I can't decide if Willow is actually low-key enough to play nice here. Jury's out.

Sunday Mahjong's Golden Gingham mat gives a nod to Willow's inner golden layer. Because it's a pretty monotone mat I like pulling a layer coordinate and introducing a new color to pop against all the golden/mustard tones.

Sorry for the pic, lol, Mary Benson doesn't have any clean photos of her mats up (don't blame her, since she is getting knocked off) so ignore the peach Benson tiles on the mat, but this mat is full of various shades of green and can accommodate Willow. That said, it's not my favorite match for these tiles or this mat.
Middle & Main Mahjong's June Bride is a sweet, simple dainty border pattern with a wide open center. If you like simple and pretty, this is a great way to go for Willow.
Bespoke Mahjong's Jungle mat in turquoise has both a range of greens, blues and golden mustard tones so Willow and Jungle will get along just fine. Bonus - this mat is double sided!

Britt Mills' Legacy mat is a fan favorite for good reason. It has a strong, fun pattern that adds just enough femininity while being grounded in deep shades of evergreen and light olive. Willow's grayed out green fits in great here.
Mahjong Row & Co's Osmanthus looks like it could have been made for Willow with both its green and gold coordination

Veranda by Britt Mills is another example of how her beautiful watercolor florals are easily matched, I love the neutral beige center of this one that gives the eye a break and allows Willow to pop more in the center.

I wanted to pull a mat from Britt Mills' latest mat drop and Quinn is really the only one that has remote coordination - so here ya go:) It's subtle and wouldn't be my 1st pick but I think the busyness of this mat makes it a fun match.
Sunday Mahjong's Rattan mat is one of my favorite mats because it's just so simple. It's green is a deeper olive and Willow is light enough to still get some contrast on this mat.

Bespoke's Year of the Dragon mat in Periwinkle has lots of greens to coordinate with Willow. I chose the Periwinkle because I like the tranquility of the light blue with the sage green and then all the fun pops of color and iconic motif. That said many of the YOTD colors could work with Willow.
Tigre de Tartan's Bunny Love is almost an exact match to Willow's back. So if you like a low contrast tonal look, this is a great match for Willow.
Similarly Tigre de Tartan's Nantucket Basket brings all the golden tones and allows Willow to have a moment of "pop"
Tigre de Tartan's new Queen Bee mat has been getting a lot of buzz...(see what I did there?)...and it's definitely a great option for Willow!

Wrapping up with some Oh My Mahjong retired mats - 1st up Soho, which is a bit more bold than Willow's vibe, but if you own it already and are adding Willow to your collection this would be a fun combo to play with.

Oh My Mahjong's Citrus Songbird has lots of pastel green within it as well as golden tones in the lemons and trellis borders and I think would look really nice with Willow if you own it or can score it second hand.
